chunks: And from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Malik ibn Zayd who said: Ziyad ibn Aqilah narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Samra al-Sawwa'i narrated to us, saying: I was with my father near the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
He said: 'After me, there will be twelve emirs.' Then he lowered his voice, so I asked my father, and he said: 'He said: All of them are from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve emirs mentioned in the hadith and what is their tribal affiliation?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani, establishes the foundational claim of twelve specific successors from Quraysh, a number that mirrors the twelve tribes of Israel and reinforces the concept of divinely appointed leadership (Imamate). In Shia scholarship, this narration is pivotal for validating the lineage of the Twelve Imams, emphasizing their Qurashite origin as a prerequisite for legitimate authority following the Prophet (SAWW).
